findings.title: Nil dereference in TopicsController#unsubscribe when TopicUser does not exist
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the logged-in user has never visited, interacted with, or been emailed about the topic (or if they visit `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` directly). Calling `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` resulting in a 500 error. Even if a `TopicUser` row exists, mutating `@topic_view` requires updating or reloading the notification level (or using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` before constructing `@topic_view`), because `@topic_view` instantiated on line 99 has already cached `@topic_user` with the old `notification_level`, so `perform_show_response` will serialize the stale notification level to the client.

findings.title: Frontend transition to topicUnsubscribe route does not actually unsubscribe the user
findings.body: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `model` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which fetches `/t/:id.json` (`TopicsController#show`) or consumes the `topic_<id>` preload from `perform_show_response`. Meanwhile, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates the `TopicUser` notification level on the `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` request itself—and does so *after* `TopicView.new` has already memoized `@topic_user` with the pre-unsubscribe `notification_level`. As a consequence: (1) on a direct page load of `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, the preloaded `TopicViewSerializer` JSON still contains the old `notification_level`, so the `topic-notifications-button` shown on the page displays the old state instead of the updated muted/regular state; and (2) if the user isn't logged in when clicking the email link or transitions to the route client-side, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is never called in JSON mode.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe action is performed on a GET request
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is routed via `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and immediately mutates `TopicUser#notification_level` in the database without user confirmation or a POST/PUT request. Email security scanners, link prefetchers, browser pre-rendering, or an `` tag on any page can trigger this GET endpoint and silently downgrade a user's topic notification level from watching/tracking to regular, or from regular to muted (and hitting it twice mutes a watched topic).
